text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

## Abstract

GSE309890 is a NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series record retrieved using the `geo_series` tool. It describes an RNA-seq (high-throughput expression profiling) study of *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 investigating how the antidepressant sertraline biases antibiotic resistance evolution through rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), implicating transketolase A (tktA) as a mutation-agnostic route to restore antibiotic susceptibility. The record was queried on the accession "GSE309890" with `list_files=true` to obtain both study metadata and the FTP-hosted supplementary file listing. The dataset comprises 6 samples (3 control replicates and 3 "adaptive evolution, 40-day" replicates) run on platform GPL24659, linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958, with a public release date of 2026/02/01. No PubMed record is currently linked to this Series. Only one downloadable supplementary file exists: `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz` (510 KB, last modified 2025-11-14), a CSV of FPKM (Fragments Per Kilobase Million) values across all 6 samples, hosted at NCBI's GEO FTP tree. GEO's E-utilities API itself returns only metadata; the actual processed expression values exist solely in this single file. This finding matters because it tells a user precisely what quantitative data is retrievable versus what remains metadata-only, avoiding wasted effort searching for raw count matrices or per-sample files that do not exist in this Series.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GEO is NCBI's public repository for functional genomics data, including both raw study metadata (title, summary, samples, platform) and links to processed data files hosted on an associated FTP directory. Studies of antibiotic resistance evolution in *E. coli* are of interest because antimicrobial resistance is a major public health concern, and this study examines an unexpected driver — SSRI antidepressant exposure — acting through central carbon metabolism (the pentose phosphate pathway) rather than through classical resistance mutations alone.

**Literature Review.** The tool result explicitly reported `pubmed_ids: []` with the note: "No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record. That means no link is registered in GEO, typically an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study. It never means the study has no data." No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Prior to this query, it was unknown (a) what the biological subject and design of GSE309890 were, and (b) which specific files, if any, are available for download versus which data exist only as unretrievable metadata.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine the content and scope of GSE309890 and to enumerate exactly which downloadable files are associated with it via the GEO FTP supplementary directory. No statistical hypothesis is tested here; this is a descriptive metadata retrieval.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** A single targeted lookup was used, routing directly to the GEO-specific tool rather than a general search, since the exact accession (GSE309890) was already known.

**Materials.** NCBI GEO, queried via the `geo_series` tool (which wraps NCBI E-utilities `esummary` against the `gds` database and separately lists the GEO FTP supplementary directory).

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)` — retrieves the Series metadata record and lists files in `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/`.

The underlying E-utilities call reported in the result was:
`https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0`

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistical analysis was performed. All counts reported (sample count = 6, supplementary file count = 1) are taken directly and verbatim from the fields `sample_count` and the length of the `supplementary_files` array in the tool's JSON response; no deduplication or derived computation was needed.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

Table 1. GSE309890 study metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Accession | GSE309890 |
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Organism | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Platform | GPL24659 |
| Sample count | 6 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Public release date | 2026/02/01 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | None |

Table 2. Samples in GSE309890

| Accession | Title |
|---|---|
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control, rep1 |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control, rep2 |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control, rep3 |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 |
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 |

Table 3. Downloadable supplementary files

| File name | Size | Last modified | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510K | 2025-11-14 11:10 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

**Findings.** GSE309890 contains 6 samples: 3 control replicates and 3 "adaptive evolution, 40-day" replicates, run on platform GPL24659 in *E. coli* K-12 MG1655. Exactly 1 supplementary file type (CSV) and 1 supplementary file entry are listed for download: `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`, a gzip-compressed CSV of FPKM values across all 6 samples, size 510K. No other processed data files (for example raw counts, BAM/BigWig tracks, or per-sample files) are listed in the supplementary directory. Zero PubMed records are linked to this Series.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The study design (3 control vs. 3 adaptive-evolution replicates) supports a two-group RNA-seq comparison consistent with the summary's description of stress-driven metabolic rewiring under long-term (40-day) adaptive evolution, though the tool result does not indicate at what stage sertraline treatment or antibiotic challenge was applied relative to the sequencing samples — only that "control" and "adaptive evolution, 40day" groups exist. The single downloadable file (an all-samples FPKM matrix) is sufficient for differential expression re-analysis but represents the only processed data product; raw reads are not part of this GEO record and would need to be retrieved separately via the associated BioProject/SRA (PRJNA1363958).

**Context.** No PubMed literature could be linked or reviewed, so the biological interpretation offered here rests solely on the Series `summary` field as authored by the submitters, not on independently retrieved peer-reviewed literature.

**Limitations.** The tool explicitly notes that "GEO's API returns metadata only" and that "the processed expression values... are not available from any E-utilities call" — they exist only in the one listed supplementary file. The `pubmed_note` further specifies that an absent PubMed link typically means the study is unpublished or not yet indexed, not that no manuscript exists. These metadata cannot establish whether additional raw sequencing data, sample attributes, or protocols exist beyond what GEO indexes; that would require querying the linked BioProject/SRA directly.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 is an unpublished (as of retrieval) 6-sample *E. coli* RNA-seq Series comparing control vs. 40-day adaptively evolved populations, with one downloadable processed file: an all-samples FPKM CSV. A worthwhile next query would be `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project("PRJNA1363958")` to determine whether raw FASTQ/SRA run files are retrievable for these same 6 samples, since GEO itself hosts no raw reads for this Series.

## References
[1] NCBI GEO, GSE309890 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP supplementary directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[3] NCBI GEO FTP series directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[4] Downloadable file: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[5] NCBI E-utilities esummary call: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0

## Acknowledgments
Data provided by NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), accessed via NCBI E-utilities and the GEO FTP archive.
